setup: How zincophilic sites govern zinc nucleation and deposition on carbon anode hosts is not established

steps.output: On zinc plating Zn-N bonds form at pyridinic-nitrogen sites, moving their chemical state toward graphitic nitrogen ; Pyridinic nitrogen, rather than graphitic nitrogen or bare graphitic carbon, is the electrochemically active zincophilic site ; Zinc adsorbs as single atoms that seed clusters, which expand into a mesoporous zinc network ; Plated zinc coexists on the carbon host as dispersed single atoms, ~1 nm clusters and extended porous networks ; Plated zinc is planar and compact on CnC HS but forms a dense mat of sharp dendritic platelets on C HS
steps.output_short: On zinc plating Zn-N bonds form at pyridinic-nitrogen sites, moving their chemical state toward graphitic nitrogen

observations: After zinc deposition the ~398 eV N 1s feature collapses and the ~401 eV feature becomes the taller of the two
The sharp 290.1 eV C 1s feature of pristine CnC HS is absent after zinc deposition, while the 284.9 and 288.3 eV features remain
The ~1200 cm-1 Raman feature weakens from the pristine trace at the top of the stack to the zinc-loaded trace at the bottom
Zinc on CnC HS is a largely flat deposit with sparse protruding platelets; on C HS the surface is a dense mat of sharp platelets
HAADF-STEM of zinc-loaded carbon shows bright zinc at three scales: isolated points, ~1 nm blobs and extended lattice-resolved patches

observations: After zinc deposition the ~398 eV N 1s feature collapses and the ~401 eV feature becomes the taller of the two
The ~1200 cm-1 Raman feature weakens from the pristine trace at the top of the stack to the zinc-loaded trace at the bottom
The two hosts' plating plateaus nearly coincide at the lowest rate and separate strongly at the highest (about -0.05 V vs -0.10 V)
Nucleation overpotentials of 39 mV and 43 mV are marked on the two initial discharge profiles
Charge transfer to zinc is more negative at every N-doped site (-0.032 to -0.037 e) than at the pristine sites (-0.023 to -0.027 e)
Electron accumulation sits as a detached lobe above zinc on pristine graphene but is denser in the zinc-substrate gap on N-doped graphene
Binding energies are +0.030/+0.014/+0.029 eV at top/hollow/bridge on pristine graphene and -0.072/-0.089/-0.077 eV on N-doped graphene
